verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David the servant of the Lord; the words which he spoke to the Lord, even the words of this Song, in the day in which the Lord delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul: and he said:
verses.2: I will love thee, O Lord, my strength.
verses.3: The Lord is my firm support, and my refuge, and my deliverer; my God is my helper, I will hope in him; he is my defender, and the horn of my salvation, and my helper.
verses.4: I will call upon the Lord with praises, and I shall be saved from mine enemies.
verses.5: The pangs of death compassed me, and the torrents of ungodliness troubled me exceedingly.
verses.6: The pangs of hell came round about me: the snares of death prevented me.
verses.7: And when I was afflicted I called upon the Lord, and cried to my God: he heard my voice out of his holy temple, and my cry shall enter before him, even into his ears.
verses.8: Then the earth shook and quaked, and the foundations of the mountains were disturbed, and were shaken, because God was angry with them.
verses.9: There went up a smoke in his wrath, and fire burst into a flame at his presence: coals were kindled at it.
verses.10: And he bowed the heaven, and came down: and thick darkness was under his feet.
verses.11: And he mounted on cherubs and flew: he flew on the wings of winds.
verses.12: And he made darkness his secret place: round about him was his tabernacle, even dark water in the clouds of the air.
verses.13: At the brightness before him the clouds passed, hail and coals of fire.
verses.14: The Lord also thundered from heaven, and the Highest uttered his voice.
verses.15: And he sent forth his weapons, and scattered them; and multiplied lightnings, and routed them.
verses.16: And the springs of waters appeared, and the foundations of the world were exposed, at thy rebuke, O Lord, at the blasting of the breath of thy wrath.
verses.17: He sent from on high and took me, he drew me to himself out of many waters.
verses.18: He will deliver me from my mighty enemies, and from them that hate me; for they are stronger than I.
verses.19: They prevented me in the day of mine affliction: but the Lord was my stay against them.
verses.20: And he brought me out into a wide place: he will deliver me, because he has pleasure in me.
verses.21: And the Lord will recompense me according to my righteousness; even according to the purity of my hands will he recompense me.
verses.22: For I have kept the ways of the Lord and have not wickedly departed from my God.
verses.23: For all his judgments were before me, and his ordinances departed not from me.
verses.24: And I shall be blameless with him, and shall keep myself from mine iniquity.
verses.25: And the Lord shall recompense me according to my righteousness, and according to the purity of my hands before his eyes.
verses.26: With the holy thou wilt be holy; and with the innocent man thou wilt be innocent.
verses.27: And with the excellent man thou wilt be excellent; and with the perverse thou wilt shew frowardness.
verses.28: For thou wilt save the lowly people, and wilt humble the eyes of the proud.
verses.29: For thou, O Lord, wilt light my lamp: my God, thou wilt lighten my darkness.
verses.30: For by thee shall I be delivered from a troop; and by my God I will pass over a wall.
verses.31: As for my God, his way is perfect: the oracles of the Lord are tried in the fire; he is a protector of all them that hope in him.
verses.32: For who is God but the Lord? and who is a God except our God?
verses.33: It is God that girds me with strength, and has made my way blameless:
verses.34: who strengthens my feet as hart's feet, and sets me upon high places.
verses.35: He instructs my hands for war; and thou hast made my arms as a brazen bow.
verses.36: And thou hast made me secure in my salvation: and thy right hand has helped me, and thy correction has upheld me to the end; yea, thy correction itself shall instruct me.
verses.37: Thou hast made room for my goings under me, and my footsteps did not fail.
verses.38: I will pursue mine enemies, and overtake them; and I will not turn back until they are consumed.
verses.39: I will dash them to pieces and they shall not be able to stand: they shall fall under my feet.
verses.40: For thou hast girded me with strength for war: thou hast beaten down under me all that rose up against me.
verses.41: And thou hast made mine enemies turn their backs before me; and thou hast destroyed them that hated me.
verses.42: They cried, but there was no deliverer: even to the Lord, but he hearkened not to them.
verses.43: I will grind them as the mud of the streets: and I will beat them small as dust before the wind.
verses.44: Deliver me from the gainsayings of the people: thou shalt make me head of the Gentiles: a people whom I knew not served me,
verses.45: at the hearing of the ear they obeyed me: the strange children lied to me.
verses.46: The strange children waxed old, and fell away from their paths through lameness.
verses.47: The Lord lives; and blessed be my God; and let the God of my salvation be exalted.
verses.48: It is God that avenges me, and has subdued the nations under me;
verses.49: my deliverer from angry enemies: thou shalt set me on high above them that rise up against me: thou shalt deliver me from the unrighteous man.
verses.50: Therefore will I confess to thee, O Lord, among the Gentiles, and sing to thy name.
verses.51: God magnifies the deliverances of his king; and deals mercifully with David his anointed, and his seed, for ever.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David.
verses.2: The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.
verses.3: Day to day utters speech, and night to night proclaims knowledge.
verses.4: There are no speeches or words, in which their voices are not heard.
verses.5: Their voice is gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
verses.6: In the sun he has set his tabernacle; and he comes forth as a bridegroom out of his chamber: he will exult as a giant to run his course.
verses.7: His going forth is from the extremity of heaven, and his circuit to the other end of heaven: and no one shall be hidden from his heat.
verses.8: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting souls: the testimony of the Lord is faithful, instructing babes.
verses.9: The ordinances of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is bright, enlightening the eyes.
verses.10: The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring for ever and ever: the judgments of the Lord are true, and justified altogether.
verses.11: To be desired more than gold, and much precious stone: sweeter also than honey and the honey-comb.
verses.12: For thy servant keeps to them: in the keeping of them there is great reward.
verses.13: Who will understand his transgressions? purge thou me from my secret sins.
verses.14: And spare thy servant the attack of strangers: if they do not gain the dominion over me, then shall I be blameless, and I shall be clear from great sin.
verses.15: So shall the sayings of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be pleasing continually before thee, O Lord my helper, and my redeemer.

verses.1: For the end, a Song of David among the Psalms.
verses.2: When I called upon him, the God of my righteousness heard me: thou hast made room for me in tribulation; pity me, and hearken to my prayer.
verses.3: O ye sons of men, how long will ye be slow of heart? wherefore do ye love vanity, and seek falsehood? Pause.
verses.4: But know ye that the Lord has done wondrous things for his holy one: the Lord will hear me when I cry to him.
verses.5: Be ye angry, and sin not; feel compunction upon your beds for what ye say in your hearts. Pause.
verses.6: Offer the sacrifice of righteousness, and trust in the Lord.
verses.7: Many say, Who will shew us good things? the light of thy countenance, O Lord, has been manifested towards us.
verses.8: Thou hast put gladness into my heart: they have been satisfied with the fruit of their corn and wine and oil.
verses.9: I will both lie down in peace and sleep: for thou, Lord, only hast caused me to dwell securely.

verses.1: For the end, concerning the wine-presses, a Psalm of David.
verses.2: O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is thy name in all the earth! for thy magnificence is exalted above the heavens.
verses.3: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou perfected praise, because of thine enemies; that thou mightest put down the enemy and avenger.
verses.4: For I will regard the heavens, the work of thy fingers; the moon and stars, which thou hast established.
verses.5: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
verses.6: Thou madest him a little less than angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour;
verses.7: and thou hast set him over the works of thy hands: thou hast put all things under his feet:
verses.8: sheep and all oxen, yea, and the cattle of the field;
verses.9: the birds of the sky, and the fish of the sea, the creatures passing through the paths of the sea.
verses.10: O Lord our Lord, how wonderful is thy name in all the earth!

verses.1: A Psalm of David, when he fled from the presence of his son Abessalom.
verses.2: O Lord, why are they that afflict me multiplied? many rise up against me.
verses.3: Many say concerning my soul, There is no deliverance for him in his God. Pause.
verses.4: But thou, O Lord, art my helper: my glory, and the one that lifts up my head.
verses.5: I cried to the Lord with my voice, and he heard me out of his holy mountain. Pause.
verses.6: I lay down and slept; I awaked; for the Lord will help me.
verses.7: I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, who beset me round about.
verses.8: Arise, Lord; deliver me, my God: for thou hast smitten all who were without cause mine enemies; thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.
verses.9: Deliverance is the Lord's, and thy blessing is upon thy people.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David, concerning her that inherits.
verses.2: Hearken to my words, O Lord, attend to my cry.
verses.3: Attend to the voice of my supplication, my King, and my God: for to thee, O Lord, will I pray.
verses.4: In the morning thou shalt hear my voice: in the morning will I wait upon thee, and will look up.
verses.5: For thou art not a God that desires iniquity; neither shall the worker of wickedness dwell with thee.
verses.6: Neither shall the transgressors continue in thy sight: thou hatest, O Lord, all them that work iniquity.
verses.7: Thou wilt destroy all that speak falsehood: the Lord abhors the bloody and deceitful man.
verses.8: But I will enter into thine house in the multitude of thy mercy: I will worship in thy fear toward thy holy temple.
verses.9: Lead me, O Lord, in thy righteousness because of mine enemies; make my way plain before thy face.
verses.10: For there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain; their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit.
verses.11: Judge them, O God; let them fail of their counsels: cast them out according to the abundance of their ungodliness; for they have provoked thee, O Lord.
verses.12: But let all that trust on thee be glad in thee: they shall exult for ever, and thou shalt dwell among them; and all that love thy name shall rejoice in thee.
verses.13: For thou, Lord, shalt bless the righteous: thou hast compassed us as with a shield of favour.

verses.1: A Psalm for David on the first day of the week. The earth is the Lord's and the fulness thereof; the world, and all that dwell in it.
verses.2: He has founded it upon the seas, and prepared it upon the rivers.
verses.3: Who shall go up to the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in his holy place?
verses.4: He that is innocent in his hands and pure in his heart; who has not lifted up his soul to vanity, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.
verses.5: He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Saviour.
verses.6: This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek the face of the God of Jacob. Pause.
verses.7: Lift up your gates, ye princes, and be ye lifted up, ye everlasting doors; and the king of glory shall come in.
verses.8: Who is this king of glory? the Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.
verses.9: Lift up your gates, ye princes; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the king of glory shall come in.
verses.10: Who is this king of glory? The Lord of hosts, he is this king of glory.

verses.1: For the end, concerning the morning aid, a Psalm of David.
verses.2: O God, my God, attend to me: why hast thou forsaken me? the account of my transgressions is far from my salvation.
verses.3: O my God, I will cry to thee by day, but thou wilt not hear: and by night, and it shall not be accounted for folly to me.
verses.4: But thou, the praise of Israel, dwellest in a sanctuary.
verses.5: Our fathers hoped in thee; they hoped, and thou didst deliver them.
verses.6: They cried to thee, and were saved: they hoped in thee, and were not ashamed.
verses.7: But I am a worm, and not a man; a reproach of men, and scorn of the people.
verses.8: All that saw me mocked me: they spoke with their lips, they shook the head, saying,
verses.9: He hoped in the Lord: let him deliver him, let him save him, because he takes pleasure in him.
verses.10: For thou art he that drew me out of the womb; my hope from my mother's breasts.
verses.11: I was cast on thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother's belly.
verses.12: Stand not aloof from me; for affliction is near; for there is no helper.
verses.13: Many bullocks have compassed me: fat bulls have beset me round.
verses.14: They have opened their mouth against me, as a ravening and roaring lion.
verses.15: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are loosened: my heart in the midst of my belly is become like melting wax.
verses.16: My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue is glued to my throat; and thou hast brought me down to the dust of death.
verses.17: For many dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked doers has beset me round: they pierced my hands and my feet.
verses.18: They counted all my bones; and they observed and looked upon me.
verses.19: They parted my garments among themselves, and cast lots upon my raiment.
verses.20: But thou, O Lord, remove not my help afar off: be ready for mine aid.
verses.21: Deliver my soul from the sword; my only-begotten one from the power of the dog.
verses.22: Save me from the lion's mouth; and regard my lowliness from the horns of the unicorns.
verses.23: I will declare thy name to my brethren: in the midst of the church will I sing praise to thee.
verses.24: Ye that fear the Lord, praise him; all ye seed of Jacob, glorify him: let all the seed of Israel fear him.
verses.25: For he has not despised nor been angry at the supplication of the poor; nor turned away his face from me; but when I cried to him, he heard me.
verses.26: My praise is of thee in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him.
verses.27: The poor shall eat and be satisfied; and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: their heart shall live for ever.
verses.28: All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before him.
verses.29: For the kingdom is the Lord's; and he is the governor of the nations.
verses.30: All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and worshipped: all that go down to the earth shall fall down before him: my soul also lives to him.
verses.31: And my seed shall serve him: the generation that is coming shall be reported to the Lord.
verses.32: And they shall report his righteousness to the people that shall be born, whom the Lord has made.

verses.1: A Psalm of David. The Lord tends me as a shepherd, and I shall want nothing.
verses.2: In a place of green grass, there he has made me dwell: he has nourished me by the water of rest.
verses.3: He has restored my soul: he has guided me into the paths of righteousness, for his name's sake.
verses.4: Yea, even if I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will not be afraid of evils: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff, these have comforted me.
verses.5: Thou hast prepared a table before me in presence of them that afflict me: thou hast thoroughly anointed my head with oil; and thy cup cheers me like the best wine.
verses.6: Thy mercy also shall follow me all the days of my life: and my dwelling shall be in the house of the Lord for a very long time.

verses.1: A Psalm of David, when he changed his countenance before Abimelech; and he let him go, and he departed.
verses.2: I will bless the Lord at all times: his praise shall be continually in my mouth.
verses.3: My soul shall boast herself in the Lord: let the meek hear, and rejoice.
verses.4: Magnify ye the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.
verses.5: I sought the Lord diligently, and he hearkened to me, and delivered me from all my sojournings.
verses.6: Draw near to him, and be enlightened: and your faces shall not by any means be ashamed.
verses.7: This poor man cried, and the Lord hearkened to him, and delivered him out of all his afflictions.
verses.8: The angel of the Lord will encamp round about them that fear him, and will deliver them.
verses.9: Taste and see that the Lord is good: blessed is the man who hopes in him.
verses.10: Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.
verses.11: The rich have become poor and hungry: but they that seek the Lord diligently shall not want any good thing. Pause.
verses.12: Come, ye children, hear me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
verses.13: What man is there that desires life, loving to see good days?
verses.14: Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.
verses.15: Turn away from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
verses.16: The eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer:
verses.17: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil, to destroy their memorial from the earth. The righteous cried, and the Lord hearkened to them,
verses.18: and delivered them out of all their afflictions.
verses.19: The Lord is near to them that are of a contrite heart; and will save the lowly in spirit.
verses.20: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but out of them all the Lord will deliver them.
verses.21: He keeps all their bones: not one of them shall be broken.
verses.22: The death of sinners is evil: and they that hate righteousness will go wrong.
verses.23: The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: and none of those that hope in him shall go wrong.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David.
verses.2: The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee.
verses.3: Send thee help from the sanctuary, and aid thee out of Sion.
verses.4: Remember all thy sacrifice, and enrich thy whole-burnt-offering. Pause.
verses.5: Grant thee according to thy heart, and fulfil all thy desire.
verses.6: We will exult in thy salvation, and in the name of our God shall we be magnified: the Lord fulfil all thy petitions.
verses.7: Now I know that the Lord has saved his Christ: he shall hear him from his holy heaven: the salvation of his right hand is mighty.
verses.8: Some glory in chariots, and some in horses: but we will glory in the name of the Lord our God.
verses.9: They are overthrown and fallen: but we are risen, and have been set upright.
verses.10: O Lord, save the king: and hear us in whatever day we call upon thee.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David, an utterance of extreme fear.
verses.2: O Lord, I have hoped in thee; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness and rescue me.
verses.3: Incline thine ear to me; make haste to rescue me: be thou to me for a protecting God, and for a house of refuge to save me.
verses.4: For thou art my strength and my refuge; and thou shalt guide me for thy name's sake, and maintain me.
verses.5: Thou shalt bring me out of the snare which they have hidden for me; for thou, O Lord, art my defender.
verses.6: Into thine hands I will commit my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O Lord God of truth.
verses.7: Thou hast hated them that idly persist in vanities: but I have hoped in the Lord.
verses.8: I will exult and be glad in thy mercy: for thou hast looked upon mine affliction; thou hast saved my soul from distresses.
verses.9: And thou hast not shut me up into the hands of the enemy: thou hast set my feet in a wide place.
verses.10: Pity me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: my eye is troubled with indignation, my soul and my belly.
verses.11: For my life is spent with grief, and my years with groanings: my strength has been weakened through poverty, and my bones are troubled.
verses.12: I became a reproach among all mine enemies, but exceedingly so to my neighbours, and a fear to mine acquaintance: they that saw me without fled from me.
verses.13: I have been forgotten as a dead man out of mind: I am become as a broken vessel.
verses.14: For I heard the slander of many that dwelt round about: when they were gathered together against me, they took counsel to take my life.
verses.15: But I hoped in thee, O Lord: I said, Thou art my God.
verses.16: My lots are in thy hands: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies,
verses.17: and from them that persecute me. Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: save me in thy mercy.
verses.18: O Lord, let me not be ashamed, for I have called upon thee: let the ungodly be ashamed, and brought down to Hades.
verses.19: Let the deceitful lips become dumb, which speak iniquity against the righteous with pride and scorn.
verses.20: How abundant is the multitude of thy goodness, O Lord, which thou hast laid up for them that fear thee! thou hast wrought it out for them that hope on thee, in the presence of the sons of men.
verses.21: Thou wilt hide them in the secret of thy presence from the vexation of man: thou wilt screen them in a tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues.
verses.22: Blessed be the Lord: for he has magnified his mercy in a fortified city.
verses.23: But I said in my extreme fear, I am cast out from the sight of thine eyes: therefore thou didst hearken, O Lord, to the voice of my supplication when I cried to thee.
verses.24: Love the Lord, all ye his saints: for the Lord seeks for truth, and renders a reward to them that deal very proudly.
verses.25: Be of good courage, and let your heart be strengthened, all ye that hope in the Lord.

verses.1: A Psalm of David for remembrance concerning the Sabbath-day.
verses.2: O Lord, rebuke me not in thy wrath, neither chasten me in thine anger.
verses.3: For thy weapons are fixed in me, and thou hast pressed thy hand heavily upon me.
verses.4: For there is no health in my flesh because of thine anger; there is no peace to my bones because of my sins.
verses.5: For my transgressions have gone over mine head: they have pressed heavily upon me like a weighty burden.
verses.6: My bruises have become noisome and corrupt, because of my foolishness.
verses.7: I have been wretched and bowed down continually: I went with a mourning countenance all the day.
verses.8: For my soul is filled with mockings; and there is no health in my flesh.
verses.9: I have been afflicted and brought down exceedingly: I have roared for the groaning of my heart.
verses.10: But all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hidden from thee.
verses.11: My heart is troubled, my strength has failed me; and the light of mine eyes is not with me.
verses.12: My friends and my neighbours drew near before me, and stood still; and my nearest of kin stood afar off.
verses.13: While they pressed hard upon me that sought my soul: and they that sought my hurt spoke vanities, and devised deceits all the day.
verses.14: But I, as a deaf man, heard not; and was as a dumb man not opening his mouth.
verses.15: And I was as a man that hears not, and who has no reproofs in his mouth.
verses.16: For I hoped in thee, O Lord: thou wilt hear, O Lord my God.
verses.17: For I said, Lest mine enemies rejoice against me: for when my feet were moved, they spoke boastingly against me.
verses.18: For I am ready for plagues, and my grief is continually before me.
verses.19: For I will declare mine iniquity, and be distressed for my sin.
verses.20: But mine enemies live, and are mightier than I: and they that hate me unjustly are multiplied.
verses.21: They that reward evil for good slandered me; because I followed righteousness.
verses.22: Forsake me not, O Lord my God: depart not from me.
verses.23: Draw nigh to my help, O Lord of my salvation.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David.
verses.2: Blessed is the man who thinks on the poor and needy: the Lord shall deliver him in an evil day.
verses.3: May the Lord preserve him and keep him alive, and bless him on the earth, and not deliver him into the hands of his enemy.
verses.4: May the Lord help him upon the bed of his pain; thou hast made all his bed in his sickness.
verses.5: I said, O Lord, have mercy upon me; heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee.
verses.6: Mine enemies have spoken evil against me, saying, When shall he die, and his name perish?
verses.7: And if he came to see me, his heart spoke vainly; he gathered iniquity to himself; he went forth and spoke in like manner.
verses.8: All my enemies whispered against me; against me they devised my hurt.
verses.9: They denounced a wicked word against me, saying, Now that he lies, shall he not rise up again?
verses.10: For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, lifted up his heel against me.
verses.11: But thou, O Lord, have compassion upon me, and raise me up, and I shall requite them.
verses.12: By this I know that thou hast delighted in me, because mine enemy shall not rejoice over me.
verses.13: But thou didst help me because of mine innocence, and hast established me before thee for ever.
verses.14: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting, and to everlasting. So be it, so be it.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm for the sons of Core.
verses.2: Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout to God with a voice of exultation.
verses.3: For the Lord most high is terrible; he is a great king over all the earth.
verses.4: He has subdued the peoples under us, and the nations under our feet.
verses.5: He has chosen out his inheritance for us, the beauty of Jacob which he loved. Pause.
verses.6: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with a sound of a trumpet.
verses.7: Sing praises to our God, sing praises: sing praises to our King, sing praises.
verses.8: For God is king of all the earth: sing praises with understanding.
verses.9: God reigns over the nations: God sits upon the throne of his holiness.
verses.10: The rulers of the people are assembled with the God of Abraam: for God's mighty ones of the earth have been greatly exalted.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm for instruction, for the sons of Core.
verses.2: O God, we have heard with our ears, our fathers have told us, the work which thou wroughtest in their days, in the days of old.
verses.3: Thine hand utterly destroyed the heathen, and thou didst plant them: thou didst afflict the nations, and cast them out.
verses.4: For they inherited not the land by their own sword, and their own arm did not deliver them; but thy right hand, and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance, because thou wert well pleased in them.
verses.5: Thou art indeed my King and my God, who commandest deliverances for Jacob.
verses.6: In thee will we push down our enemies, and in thy name will we bring to nought them that rise up against us.
verses.7: For I will not trust in my bow, and my sword shall not save me.
verses.8: For thou hast saved us from them that afflicted us, and hast put to shame them that hated us.
verses.9: In God will we make our boast all the day, and to thy name will we give thanks for ever. Pause.
verses.10: But now thou hast cast off, and put us to shame; and thou wilt not go forth with our hosts.
verses.11: Thou hast turned us back before our enemies; and they that hated us spoiled for themselves.
verses.12: Thou madest us as sheep for meat; and thou scatteredst us among the nations.
verses.13: Thou hast sold thy people without price, and there was no profit by their exchange.
verses.14: Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.
verses.15: Thou hast made us a proverb among the Gentiles, a shaking of the head among the nations.
verses.16: All the day my shame is before me, and the confusion of my face has covered me,
verses.17: because of the voice of the slanderer and reviler; because of the enemy and avenger.
verses.18: All these things are come upon us: but we have not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt unrighteously in thy covenant.
verses.19: And our heart has not gone back; but thou hast turned aside our paths from thy way.
verses.20: For thou hast laid us low in a place of affliction, and the shadow of death has covered us.
verses.21: If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread out our hands to a strange god; shall not God search these things out?
verses.22: for he knows the secrets of the heart.
verses.23: For, for thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for slaughter.
verses.24: Awake, wherefore sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, and do not cast us off for ever.
verses.25: Wherefore turnest thou thy face away, and forgettest our poverty and our affliction?
verses.26: For our soul has been brought down to the dust; our belly has cleaved to the earth.
verses.27: Arise, O Lord, help us, and redeem us for thy name's sake.

verses.1: For the end, for the sons of Core; a Psalm concerning secret things.
verses.2: God is our refuge and strength, a help in the afflictions that have come heavily upon us.
verses.3: Therefore will we not fear when the earth is troubled, and the mountains are removed into the depths of the seas.
verses.4: Their waters have roared and been troubled, the mountains have been troubled by his might. Pause.
verses.5: The flowings of the river gladden the city of God: the Most High has sanctified his tabernacle.
verses.6: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her with his countenance.
verses.7: The nations were troubled, the kingdoms tottered: he uttered his voice, the earth shook.
verses.8: The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our helper. Pause.
verses.9: Come, and behold the works of the Lord, what wonders he has achieved on the earth.
verses.10: Putting an end to wars as for the ends of the earth; he will crush the bow, and break in pieces the weapon, and burn the bucklers with fire.
verses.11: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.
verses.12: The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our helper.

verses.1: For the end, for alternate strains by the sons of Core; for instruction, a Song concerning the beloved.
verses.2: My heart has uttered a good matter: I declare my works to the king: my tongue is the pen of a quick writer.
verses.3: Thou art more beautiful than the sons of men: grace has been shed forth on thy lips: therefore God has blessed thee for ever.
verses.4: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O Mighty One, in thy comeliness, and in thy beauty;
verses.5: and bend thy bow, and prosper, and reign, because of truth and meekness and righteousness; and thy right hand shall guide thee wonderfully.
verses.6: Thy weapons are sharpened, Mighty One, (the nations shall fall under thee) they are in the heart of the king's enemies.
verses.7: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of righteousness.
verses.8: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity: therefore God, thy God, has anointed thee with the oil of gladness beyond thy fellows.
verses.9: Myrrh, and stacte, and cassia are exhaled from thy garments, and out of the ivory palaces,
verses.10: with which kings' daughters have gladdened thee for thine honour: the queen stood by on thy right hand, clothed in vesture wrought with gold, and arrayed in divers colours.
verses.11: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear; forget also thy people, and thy father's house.
verses.12: Because the king has desired thy beauty; for he is thy Lord.
verses.13: And the daughter of Tyre shall adore him with gifts; the rich of the people of the land shall supplicate thy favour.
verses.14: All her glory is that of the daughter of the king of Esebon, robed as she is in golden fringed garments,
verses.15: in embroidered clothing: virgins shall be brought to the king after her: her fellows shall be brought to thee.
verses.16: They shall be brought with gladness and exultation: they shall be led into the king's temple.
verses.17: Instead of thy fathers children are born to thee: thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.
verses.18: They shall make mention of thy name from generation to generation: therefore shall the nations give thanks to thee for ever, even for ever and ever.

verses.1: A Psalm of praise for the sons of Core on the second day of the week.
verses.2: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
verses.3: The city of the great King is well planted on the mountains of Sion, with the joy of the whole earth, on the sides of the north.
verses.4: God is known in her palaces, when he undertakes to help her.
verses.5: For, behold, the kings of the earth were assembled, they came together.
verses.6: They saw, and so they wondered: they were troubled, they were moved.
verses.7: Trembling took hold on them: there were the pangs as of a woman in travail.
verses.8: Thou wilt break the ships of Tharsis with a vehement wind.
verses.9: As we have heard, so have we also seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: God has founded it for ever. Pause.
verses.10: We have thought of thy mercy, O God, in the midst of thy people.
verses.11: According to thy name, O God, so is also thy praise to the ends of the earth: thy right hand is full of righteousness.
verses.12: Let mount Sion rejoice, let the daughters of Judæa exult, because of thy judgments, O Lord.
verses.13: Go round about Sion, and encompass her: tell ye her towers.
verses.14: Mark ye well her strength, and observe her palaces; that ye may tell the next generation.
verses.15: For this is our God for ever and ever: he will be our guide for evermore.

verses.1: For the end, concerning the people that were removed from the sanctuary, by David for a memorial, when the Philistines caught him in Geth.
verses.2: Have mercy upon me, O God; for man has trodden me down; all the day long he warring has afflicted me.
verses.3: Mine enemies have trodden me down all the day from the dawning of the day; for there are many warring against me.
verses.4: They shall be afraid, but I will trust in thee.
verses.5: In God I will praise my words; all the day have I hoped in God; I will not fear what flesh shall do to me.
verses.6: All the day long they have abominated my words; all their devices are against me for evil.
verses.7: They will dwell near and hide themselves; they will watch my steps, accordingly as I have waited patiently in my soul.
verses.8: Thou wilt on no account save them; thou wilt bring down the people in wrath.
verses.9: O God, I have declared my life to thee; thou hast set my tears before thee, even according to thy promise.
verses.10: Mine enemies shall be turned back, in the day wherein I shall call upon thee; behold, I know that thou art my God.
verses.11: In God will I praise his word; in the Lord will I praise his saying.
verses.12: I have hoped in God; I will not be afraid of what man shall do to me.
verses.13: The vows of thy praise, O God, which I will pay, are upon me.
verses.14: For thou hast delivered my soul from death, and my feet from sliding, that I should be well-pleasing before God in the land of the living.

verses.1: For the end. Destroy not: by David, for a memorial, when he fled from the presence of Saul to the cave.
verses.2: Have mercy, upon me, O God, have mercy upon me: for my soul has trusted in thee: and in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, until the iniquity have passed away.
verses.3: I will cry to God most high; the God who has benefited me. Pause.
verses.4: He sent from heaven and saved me; he gave to reproach them that trampled on me: God has sent forth his mercy and his truth;
verses.5: and he has delivered my soul from the midst of lions' whelps: I lay down to sleep, though troubled. As for the sons of men, their teeth are arms and missile weapons, and their tongue a sharp sword.
verses.6: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; and thy glory above all the earth.
verses.7: They have prepared snares for my feet, and have bowed down my soul: they have dug a pit before my face, and fallen into it themselves. Pause.
verses.8: My heart, O God, is ready, my heart is ready: I will sing, yea will sing psalms.
verses.9: Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I will awake early.
verses.10: O Lord, I will give thanks to thee among the nations: I will sing to thee among the Gentiles.
verses.11: For thy mercy has been magnified even to the heavens, and thy truth to the clouds.
verses.12: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; and thy glory above all the earth.

verses.1: For the end, among Hymns of instruction by David.
verses.2: Hearken, O God, to my prayer; and disregard not my supplication.
verses.3: Attend to me, and hearken to me: I was grieved in my meditation, and troubled;
verses.4: because of the voice of the enemy, and because of the oppression of the sinner: for they brought iniquity against me, and were wrathfully angry with me.
verses.5: My heart was troubled within me; and the fear of death fell upon me.
verses.6: Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me.
verses.7: And I said, O that I had wings as those of a dove! then would I flee away, and be at rest.
verses.8: Lo! I have fled afar off, and lodged in the wilderness. Pause.
verses.9: I waited for him that should deliver me from distress of spirit and tempest.
verses.10: Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongues: for I have seen iniquity and gainsaying in the city.
verses.11: Day and night he shall go round about it upon its walls: iniquity and sorrow and unrighteousness are in the midst of it;
verses.12: and usury and craft have not failed from its streets.
verses.13: For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have endured it; and if one who hated me had spoken vauntingly against me, I would have hid myself from him.
verses.14: But thou, O man likeminded, my guide, and my acquaintance,
verses.15: who in companionship with me sweetened our food: we walked in the house of God in concord.
verses.16: Let death come upon them, and let them go down alive into Hades, for iniquity is in their dwellings, in the midst of them.
verses.17: I cried to God, and the Lord hearkened to me.
verses.18: Evening, and morning, and at noon I will declare and make known my wants: and he shall hear my voice.
verses.19: He shall deliver my soul in peace from them that draw nigh to me: for they were with me in many cases.
verses.20: God shall hear, and bring them low, even he that has existed from eternity. Pause. For they suffer no reverse, and therefore they have not feared God.
verses.21: He has reached forth his hand for retribution; they have profaned his covenant.
verses.22: They were scattered at the anger of his countenance, and his heart drew nigh them. His words were smoother than oil, yet are they darts.
verses.23: Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee; he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
verses.24: But thou, O God, shalt bring them down to the pit of destruction; bloody and crafty men shall not live out half their days; but I will hope in thee, O Lord.

verses.1: For the end, for them that shall yet be changed; for an inscription by David for instruction,
verses.2: when he had burned Mesopotamia of Syria, and Syria Sobal, and Joab had returned and smitten in the valley of salt twelve thousand.
verses.3: O God, thou hast rejected and destroyed us; thou hast been angry, yet hast pitied us.
verses.4: Thou hast shaken the earth, and troubled it; heal its breaches, for it has been shaken.
verses.5: Thou hast shewn thy people hard things: thou hast made us drink the wine of astonishment.
verses.6: Thou hast given a token to them that fear thee, that they might flee from the bow. Pause.
verses.7: That thy beloved ones may be delivered; save with thy right hand, and hear me.
verses.8: God has spoken in his holiness; I will rejoice, and divide Sicima, and measure out the valley of tents.
verses.9: Galaad is mine, and Manasse is mine; and Ephraim is the strength of my head;
verses.10: Judas is my king; Moab is the caldron of my hope; over Idumea will I stretch out my shoe; the Philistines have been subjected to me.
verses.11: Who will lead me into the fortified city? who will guide me as far as Idumea?
verses.12: Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our forces?
verses.13: Give us help from trouble: for vain is the deliverance of man.
verses.14: In God will we do valiantly; and he shall bring to nought them that harass us.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of instruction by David,
verses.2: when Doec the Idumean came and told Saul, and said to him, David is gone to the house of Abimelech.
verses.3: Why dost thou, O mighty man, boast of iniquity in thy mischief? All the day
verses.4: thy tongue has devised unrighteousness; like a sharpened razor thou hast wrought deceit.
verses.5: Thou hast loved wickedness more than goodness; unrighteousness better than to speak righteousness. Pause.
verses.6: Thou hast loved all words of destruction, and a deceitful tongue.
verses.7: Therefore may God destroy thee for ever, may he pluck thee up and utterly remove thee from thy dwelling, and thy root from the land of the living. Pause.
verses.8: And the righteous shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say,
verses.9: Behold the man who made not God his help; but trusted in the abundance of his wealth, and strengthened himself in his vanity.
verses.10: But I am as a fruitful olive in the house of God: I have trusted in the mercy of God for ever, even for evermore.
verses.11: I will give thanks to thee for ever, for thou hast done it: and I will wait on thy name; for it is good before thy saints.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David for Idithun.
verses.2: Shall not my soul be subjected to God? for of him is my salvation.
verses.3: For he is my God and my Saviour; my helper, I shall not be moved very much.
verses.4: How long will ye assault a man? ye are all slaughtering as with a bowed wall and a broken hedge.
verses.5: They only took counsel to set at nought mine honour: I ran in thirst: with their mouth they blessed, but with their heart they cursed. Pause.
verses.6: Nevertheless do thou, my soul, be subjected to God; for of him is my patient hope.
verses.7: For he is my God and my Saviour; my helper, I shall not be moved.
verses.8: In God is my salvation and my glory: he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.
verses.9: Hope in him, all ye congregation of the people; pour out your hearts before him, for God is our helper. Pause.
verses.10: But the sons of men are vain; the sons of men are false, so as to be deceitful in the balances; they are all alike formed out of vanity.
verses.11: Trust not in unrighteousness, and lust not after robberies: if wealth should flow in, set not your heart upon it.
verses.12: God has spoken once, and I have heard these two things, that power is of God;
verses.13: and mercy is thine, O Lord; for thou wilt recompense every one according to his works.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of a Song by David.
verses.2: Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; and let them that hate him flee from before him.
verses.3: As smoke vanishes, let them vanish: as wax melts before the fire, so let the sinners perish from before God.
verses.4: But let the righteous rejoice; let them exult before God: let them be delighted with joy.
verses.5: Sing to God, sing praises to his name: make a way for him that rides upon the west (the Lord is his name) and exult before him. They shall be troubled before the face of him,
verses.6: who is the father of the orphans, and judge of the widows: such is God in his holy place.
verses.7: God settles the solitary in a house; leading forth prisoners mightily, also them that act provokingly, even them that dwell in tombs.
verses.8: O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people, when thou wentest through the wilderness; Pause:
verses.9: the earth quaked, yea, the heavens dropped water at the presence of the God of Sina, at the presence of the God of Israel.
verses.10: O God, thou wilt grant to thine inheritance a gracious rain; for it was weary, but thou didst refresh it.
verses.11: Thy creatures dwell in it: thou hast in thy goodness prepared for the poor.
verses.12: The Lord God will give a word to them that preach it in a great company.
verses.13: The king of the forces of the beloved, of the beloved, will even grant them for the beauty of the house to divide the spoils.
verses.14: Even if ye should lie among the lots, ye shall have the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her breast with yellow gold.
verses.15: When the heavenly One scatters kings upon it, they shall be made snow-white in Selmon.
verses.16: The mountain of God is a rich mountain; a swelling mountain, a rich mountain.
verses.17: Wherefore do ye conceive evil, ye swelling mountains? this is the mountain which God has delighted to dwell in; yea, the Lord will dwell in it for ever.
verses.18: The chariots of God are ten thousand fold, thousands of rejoicing ones: the Lord is among them, in Sina, in the holy place.
verses.19: Thou art gone up on high, thou hast led captivity captive, thou hast received gifts for man, yea, for they were rebellious, that thou mightest dwell among them.
verses.20: Blessed be the Lord God, blessed be the Lord daily; and the God of our salvation shall prosper us. Pause.
verses.21: Our God is the God of salvation; and to the Lord belong the issues from death.
verses.22: But God shall crush the heads of his enemies; the hairy crown of them that go on in their trespasses.
verses.23: The Lord said, I will bring again from Basan, I will bring my people again through the depths of the sea.
verses.24: That thy foot may be dipped in blood, and the tongue of thy dogs be stained with that of thine enemies.
verses.25: Thy goings, O God, have been seen; the goings of my God, the king, in the sanctuary.
verses.26: The princes went first, next before the players on instruments, in the midst of damsels playing on timbrels.
verses.27: Praise God in the congregations, the Lord from the fountains of Israel.
verses.28: There is Benjamin the younger one in ecstasy, the princes of Juda their rulers, the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.
verses.29: O God, command thou thy strength: strengthen, O God, this which thou hast wrought in us.
verses.30: Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents to thee.
verses.31: Rebuke the wild beasts of the reed: let the crowd of bulls with the heifers of the nations be rebuked, so that they who have been proved with silver may not be shut out: scatter thou the nations that wish for wars.
verses.32: Ambassadors shall arrive out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall hasten to stretch out her hand readily to God.
verses.33: Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth; sing psalms to the Lord. Pause.
verses.34: Sing to God that rides on the heaven of heaven, eastward: lo, he will utter a mighty sound with his voice.
verses.35: Give ye glory to God: his excellency is over Israel, and his power is in the clouds.
verses.36: God is wonderful in his holy places, the God of Israel: he will give power and strength to his people: blessed be God.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David among the Hymns.
verses.2: God be merciful to us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us. Pause.
verses.3: That men may know thy way on the earth, thy salvation among all nations.
verses.4: Let the nations, O God, give thanks to thee; let all the nations give thanks to thee.
verses.5: Let the nations rejoice and exult, for thou shalt judge the peoples in equity, and shalt guide the nations on the earth. Pause.
verses.6: Let the peoples, O God, give thanks to thee; let all the peoples give thanks to thee.
verses.7: The earth has yielded her fruit; let God, our God, bless us.
verses.8: Let God bless us; and let all the ends of the earth fear him.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm and Song of David.
verses.2: Praise becomes thee, O God, in Sion; and to thee shall the vow be performed.
verses.3: Hear my prayer; to thee all flesh shall come.
verses.4: The words of transgressors have overpowered us; but do thou pardon our sins.
verses.5: Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen and adopted; he shall dwell in thy courts; we shall be filled with the good things of thy house; thy temple is holy.
verses.6: Thou art wonderful in righteousness. Hearken to us, O God our Saviour; the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are on the sea afar off:
verses.7: who dost establish the mountains in thy strength, being girded about with power;
verses.8: who troublest the depth of the sea, the sounds of its waves.
verses.9: The nations shall be troubled, and they that inhabit the ends of the earth shall be afraid of thy signs; thou wilt cause the outgoings of morning and evening to rejoice.
verses.10: Thou hast visited the earth, and saturated it; thou hast abundantly enriched it. The river of God is filled with water; thou hast prepared their food, for thus is the preparation of it.
verses.11: Saturate her furrows, multiply her fruits; the crop springing up shall rejoice in its drops.
verses.12: Thou wilt bless the crown of the year because of thy goodness; and thy plains shall be filled with fatness.
verses.13: The mountains of the wilderness shall be enriched; and the hills shall gird themselves with joy.
verses.14: The rams of the flock are clothed with wool, and the valleys shall abound in corn; they shall cry aloud, yea they shall sing hymns.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm of David, for alternate strains.
verses.2: Save me, O God; for the waters have come in to my soul.
verses.3: I am stuck fast in deep mire, and there is no standing: I am come in to the depths of the sea, and a storm has overwhelmed me.
verses.4: I am weary of crying, my throat has become hoarse; mine eyes have failed by my waiting on my God.
verses.5: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: my enemies that persecute me unrighteously are strengthened: then I restored that which I took not away.
verses.6: O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my transgressions are not hidden from thee.
verses.7: Let not them that wait on thee, O Lord of hosts, be ashamed on my account: let not them that seek thee, be ashamed on my account, O God of Israel.
verses.8: For I have suffered reproach for thy sake; shame has covered my face.
verses.9: I became strange to my brethren, and a stranger to my mother's children.
verses.10: For the zeal of thine house has eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
verses.11: And I bowed down my soul with fasting, and that was made my reproach.
verses.12: And I put on sackcloth for my covering; and I became a proverb to them.
verses.13: They that sit in the gate talked against me, and they that drank wine sang against me.
verses.14: But I will cry to thee, O Lord, in my prayer; O God, it is a propitious time: in the multitude of thy mercy hear me, in the truth of thy salvation.
verses.15: Save me from the mire, that I stick not in it: let me be delivered from them that hate me, and from the deep waters.
verses.16: Let not the waterflood drown me, nor let the deep swallow me up; neither let the well shut its mouth upon me.
verses.17: Hear me, O Lord; for thy mercy is good: according to the multitude of thy compassions look upon me.
verses.18: And turn not away thy face from thy servant; for I am afflicted: hear me speedily.
verses.19: Draw nigh to my soul and redeem it: deliver me because of mine enemies.
verses.20: For thou knowest my reproach, and my shame, and my confusion; all that afflict me are before thee.
verses.21: My soul has waited for reproach and misery; and I waited for one to grieve with me, but there was none; and for one to comfort me, but I found none.
verses.22: They gave me also gall for my food, and made me drink vinegar for my thirst.
verses.23: Let their table before them be for a snare, and for a recompence, and for a stumbling-block.
verses.24: Let their eyes be darkened that they should not see; and bow down their back continually.
verses.25: Pour out thy wrath upon them, and let the fury of thine anger take hold on them.
verses.26: Let their habitation be made desolate; and let there be no inhabitant in their tents:
verses.27: because they persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; and they have added to the grief of my wounds.
verses.28: Add iniquity to their iniquity; and let them not come into thy righteousness.
verses.29: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and let them not be written with the righteous.
verses.30: I am poor and sorrowful; but the salvation of thy countenance has helped me.
verses.31: I will praise the name of my God with a song, I will magnify him with praise;
verses.32: and this shall please God more than a young calf having horns and hoofs.
verses.33: Let the poor see and rejoice; seek the Lord diligently, and ye shall live.
verses.34: For the Lord hears the poor, and does not set at nought his fettered ones.
verses.35: Let the heavens and the earth praise him, the sea, and all things moving in them.
verses.36: For God will save Sion, and the cities of Judea shall be built; and men shall dwell there, and inherit it.
verses.37: And the seed of his servants shall possess it, and they that love his name shall dwell therein.

verses.1: For the end, among the Hymns, a Psalm for Asaph; a Song for the Assyrian.
verses.2: God is known in Judea; his name is great in Israel.
verses.3: And his place has been in peace, and his dwelling-place in Sion.
verses.4: There he broke the power of the bows, the shield, and the sword, and the battle. Pause.
verses.5: Thou dost wonderfully shine forth from the everlasting mountains.
verses.6: All the simple ones in heart were troubled; all the men of wealth have slept their sleep, and have found nothing in their hands.
verses.7: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, the riders on horses slumbered.
verses.8: Thou art terrible; and who shall withstand thee, because of thine anger?
verses.9: Thou didst cause judgment to be heard from heaven; the earth feared, and was still,
verses.10: when God arose to judgment, to save all the meek in heart. Pause.
verses.11: For the inward thought of man shall give thanks to thee: and the memorial of his inward thought shall keep a feast to thee.
verses.12: Vow, and pay your vows to the Lord our God; all that are round about him shall bring gifts, even to him that is terrible,
verses.13: and that takes away the spirits of princes; to him that is terrible among the kings of the earth.

verses.1: For the end, for alternate strains, a testimony for Asaph, a Psalm concerning the Assyrian.
verses.2: Attend, O Shepherd of Israel, who guidest Joseph like a flock; thou who sittest upon the cherubs, manifest thyself;
verses.3: before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasse, stir up thy power, and come to deliver us.
verses.4: Turn us, O God, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be delivered.
verses.5: O Lord God of hosts, how long art thou angry with the prayer of thy servant?
verses.6: Thou wilt feed us with bread of tears; and wilt cause us to drink tears by measure.
verses.7: Thou hast made us a strife to our neighbours; and our enemies have mocked at us.
verses.8: Turn us, O Lord God of hosts, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved. Pause.
verses.9: Thou hast transplanted a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it.
verses.10: Thou madest a way before it, and didst cause its roots to strike, and the land was filled with it.
verses.11: Its shadow covered the mountains, and its shoots equalled the goodly cedars.
verses.12: It sent forth its branches to the sea, and its shoots to the river.
verses.13: Wherefore hast thou broken down its hedge, while all that pass by the way pluck it?
verses.14: The boar out of the wood has laid it waste, and the wild beast has devoured it.
verses.15: O God of hosts, turn, we pray thee: look on us from heaven, and behold and visit this vine;
verses.16: and restore that which thy right hand has planted: and look on the son of man whom thou didst strengthen for thyself.
verses.17: It is burnt with fire and dug up: they shall perish at the rebuke of thy presence.
verses.18: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand, and upon the son of man whom thou didst strengthen for thyself.
verses.19: So will we not depart from thee: thou shalt quicken us, and we will call upon thy name.
verses.20: Turn us, O Lord God of hosts, and make thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.

verses.1: For the end, a Psalm for the sons of Core.
verses.2: O Lord, thou hast taken pleasure in thy land: thou hast turned back the captivity of Jacob.
verses.3: Thou hast forgiven thy people their transgressions; thou hast covered all their sins. Pause.
verses.4: Thou hast caused all thy wrath to cease: thou hast turned from thy fierce anger.
verses.5: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and turn thine anger away from us.
verses.6: Wouldest thou be angry with us for ever? or wilt thou continue thy wrath from generation to generation?
verses.7: O God, thou wilt turn and quicken us; and thy people shall rejoice in thee.
verses.8: Shew us thy mercy, O Lord, and grant us thy salvation.
verses.9: I will hear what the Lord God will say concerning me: for he shall speak peace to his people, and to his saints, and to those that turn their heart toward him.
verses.10: Moreover his salvation is near them that fear him; that glory may dwell in our land.
verses.11: Mercy and truth are met together: righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
verses.12: Truth has sprung out of the earth; and righteousness has looked down from heaven.
verses.13: For the Lord will give goodness; and our land shall yield her fruit.
verses.14: Righteousness shall go before him; and shall set his steps in the way.

verses.1: A Psalm for Asaph. God stands in the assembly of gods; and in the midst of them will judge gods.
verses.2: How long will ye judge unrighteously, and accept the persons of sinners? Pause.
verses.3: Judge the orphan and poor: do justice to the low and needy.
verses.4: Rescue the needy, and deliver the poor out of the hand of the sinner.
verses.5: They know not, nor understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth shall be shaken.
verses.6: I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you children of the Most High.
verses.7: But ye die as men, and fall as one of the princes.
verses.8: Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.

verses.1: A Psalm of a Song for the sons of Core. His foundations are in the holy mountains.
verses.2: The Lord loves the gates of Sion, more than all the tabernacles of Jacob.
verses.3: Glorious things have been spoken of thee, O city of God. Pause.
verses.4: I will make mention of Raab and Babylon to them that know me: behold also the Philistines, and Tyre, and the people of the Ethiopians: these were born there.
verses.5: A man shall say, Sion is my mother; and such a man was born in her; and the Highest himself has founded her.
verses.6: The Lord shall recount it in the writing of the people, and of these princes that were born in her. Pause.
verses.7: The dwelling of all within thee is as the dwelling of those that rejoice.

verses.1: A song of a Psalm for the sons of Core for the end, upon Maeleth for responsive strains, of instruction for Æman the Israelite.
verses.2: O Lord God of my salvation, I have cried by day and in the night before thee.
verses.3: Let my prayer come in before thee; incline thine ear to my supplication, O Lord.
verses.4: For my soul is filled with troubles, and my life has drawn nigh to Hades.
verses.5: I have been reckoned with them that go down to the pit; I became as a man without help;
verses.6: free among the dead, as the slain ones cast out, who sleep in the tomb; whom thou rememberest no more; and they are rejected from thy hand.
verses.7: They laid me in the lowest pit, in dark places, and in the shadow of death.
verses.8: Thy wrath has pressed heavily upon me, and thou hast brought upon me all thy billows. Pause.
verses.9: Thou hast removed my acquaintance far from me; they have made me an abomination to themselves; I have been delivered up, and have not gone forth.
verses.10: Mine eyes are dimmed from poverty; but I cried to thee, O Lord, all the day; I spread forth my hands to thee.
verses.11: Wilt thou work wonders for the dead? or shall physicians raise them up, that they shall praise thee?
verses.12: Shall any one declare thy mercy in the tomb? and thy truth in destruction?
verses.13: Shall thy wonders be known in darkness? and thy righteousness in a forgotten land?
verses.14: But I cried to thee, O Lord; and in the morning shall my prayer prevent thee.
verses.15: Wherefore, O Lord, dost thou reject my prayer, and turn thy face away from me?
verses.16: I am poor and in troubles from my youth; and having been exalted, I was brought low and into despair.
verses.17: Thy wrath has passed over me; and thy terrors have greatly disquieted me.
verses.18: They compassed me like water; all the day they beset me together.
verses.19: Thou hast put far from me every friend, and mine acquaintances because of my wretchedness.

verses.1: A Psalm of a Song for the Sabbath-day.
verses.2: It is a good thing to give thanks to the Lord, and to sing praises to thy name, O thou Most High;
verses.3: to proclaim thy mercy in the morning, and thy truth by night,
verses.4: on a psaltery of ten strings, with a song on the harp.
verses.5: For thou, O Lord, hast made me glad with thy work: and in the operations of thy hands will I exult.
verses.6: How have thy works been magnified, O Lord! thy thoughts are very deep.
verses.7: A foolish man will not know, and a senseless man will not understand this.
verses.8: When the sinners spring up as the grass, and all the workers of iniquity have watched; it is that they may be utterly destroyed for ever.
verses.9: But thou, O Lord, art most high for ever.
verses.10: For, behold, thine enemies shall perish; and all the workers of iniquity shall be scattered.
verses.11: But my horn shall be exalted as the horn of a unicorn; and mine old age with rich mercy.
verses.12: And mine eye has seen mine enemies, and mine ear shall hear the wicked that rise up against me.
verses.13: The righteous shall flourish as a palm-tree: he shall be increased as the cedar in Libanus.
verses.14: They that are planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of our God.
verses.15: Then shall they be increased in a fine old age; and they shall be prosperous; that they may declare
verses.16: that the Lord my God is righteous, and there is no iniquity in him.

verses.1: A Prayer for the Poor; when he is deeply afflicted, and pours out his supplication before the Lord.
verses.2: Hear my prayer, O Lord, and let my cry come to thee.
verses.3: Turn not away thy face from me: in the day when I am afflicted, incline thine ear to me: in the day when I shall call upon thee, speedily hear me.
verses.4: For my days have vanished like smoke, and my bones have been parched like a stick.
verses.5: I am blighted like grass, and my heart is dried up; for I have forgotten to eat my bread.
verses.6: By reason of the voice of my groaning, my bone has cleaved to my flesh.
verses.7: I have become like a pelican of the wilderness;
verses.8: I have become like an owl in a ruined house. I have watched, and am become as a sparrow dwelling alone on a roof.
verses.9: All the day long mine enemies have reproached me; and they that praised me have sworn against me.
verses.10: For I have eaten ashes as it were bread, and mingled my drink with weeping;
verses.11: because of thine anger and thy wrath: for thou hast lifted me up, and dashed me down.
verses.12: My days have declined like a shadow; and I am withered like grass.
verses.13: But thou, Lord, endurest for ever, and thy memorial to generation and generation.
verses.14: Thou shalt arise, and have mercy upon Sion: for it is time to have mercy upon her, for the set time is come.
verses.15: For thy servants have taken pleasure in her stones, and they shall pity her dust.
verses.16: So the nations shall fear thy name, O Lord, and all kings thy glory.
verses.17: For the Lord shall build up Sion, and shall appear in his glory.
verses.18: He has had regard to the prayer of the lowly, and has not despised their petition.
verses.19: Let this be written for another generation; and the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord.
verses.20: For he has looked out from the height of his sanctuary; the Lord looked upon the earth from heaven;
verses.21: to hear the groaning of the fettered ones, to loosen the sons of the slain;
verses.22: to proclaim the name of the Lord in Sion, and his praise in Jerusalem;
verses.23: when the people are gathered together, and the kings, to serve the Lord.
verses.24: He answered him in the way of his strength: tell me the fewness of my days.
verses.25: Take me not away in the midst of my days: thy years are through all generations.
verses.26: In the beginning thou, O Lord, didst lay the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands.
verses.27: They shall perish, but thou remainest: and they all shall wax old as a garment; and as a vesture shalt thou fold them, and they shall be changed.
verses.28: But thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.
verses.29: The children of thy servants shall dwell securely, and their seed shall prosper for ever.

verses.1: Alleluia. Give thanks to the Lord, and call upon his name; declare his works among the heathen.
verses.2: Sing to him, yea, sing praises to him: tell forth all his wonderful works.
verses.3: Glory in his holy name: let the heart of them that seek the Lord rejoice.
verses.4: Seek ye the Lord, and be strengthened; seek his face continually.
verses.5: Remember his wonderful works that he has done; his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth;
verses.6: ye seed of Abraam, his servants, ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
verses.7: He is the Lord our God; his judgments are in all the earth.
verses.8: He has remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded for a thousand generations:
verses.9: which he established as a covenant to Abraam, and he remembered his oath to Isaac.
verses.10: And he established it to Jacob for an ordinance, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant;
verses.11: saying, To thee will I give the land of Chanaan, the line of your inheritance:
verses.12: when they were few in number, very few, and sojourners in it.
verses.13: And they went from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people.
verses.14: He suffered no man to wrong them; and he rebuked kings for their sakes:
verses.15: saying, Touch not my anointed ones; and do my prophets no harm.
verses.16: Moreover he called for a famine upon the land; he broke the whole support of bread.
verses.17: He sent a man before them; Joseph was sold for a slave.
verses.18: They hurt his feet with fetters; his soul passed into iron,
verses.19: until the time that his cause came on; the word of the Lord tried him as fire.
verses.20: The king sent and loosed him; even the prince of the people, and let him go free.
verses.21: He made him lord over his house, and ruler of all his substance;
verses.22: to chastise his rulers at his pleasure, and to teach his elders wisdom.
verses.23: Israel also came into Egypt, and Jacob sojourned in the land of Cham.
verses.24: And he increased his people greatly, and made them stronger than their enemies.
verses.25: And he turned their heart to hate his people, to deal craftily with his servants.
verses.26: He sent forth Moses his servant, and Aaron whom he had chosen.
verses.27: He established among them his signs, and his wonders in the land of Cham.
verses.28: He sent forth darkness, and made it dark; yet they rebelled against his words.
verses.29: He turned their waters into blood, and slew their fish.
verses.30: Their land produced frogs abundantly, in the chambers of their kings.
verses.31: He spoke, and the dog-fly came, and lice in all their coasts.
verses.32: He turned their rain into hail, and sent flaming fire in their land.
verses.33: And he smote their vines and their fig-trees; and broke every tree of their coast.
verses.34: He spoke, and the locust came, and caterpillars innumerable,
verses.35: and devoured all the grass in their land, and devoured the fruit of their ground.
verses.36: He smote also every first-born of their land, the first-fruits of all their labour.
verses.37: And he brought them out with silver and gold; and there was not a feeble one among their tribes.
verses.38: Egypt rejoiced at their departing; for the fear of them fell upon them.
verses.39: He spread out a cloud for a covering to them, and fire to give them light by night.
verses.40: They asked, and the quail came, and he satisfied them with the bread of heaven.
verses.41: He clave the rock, and the waters flowed; rivers ran in dry places.
verses.42: For he remembered his holy word, which he promised to Abraam his servant.
verses.43: And he brought out his people with exultation, and his chosen with joy;
verses.44: and gave them the lands of the heathen; and they inherited the labours of the people;
verses.45: that they might keep his ordinances, and diligently seek his law.

verses.1: For David, when his land is established. The Lord reigns, let the earth exult, let many islands rejoice.
verses.2: Cloud and darkness are round about him; righteousness and judgment are the establishment of his throne.
verses.3: Fire shall go before him, and burn up his enemies round about.
verses.4: His lightnings appeared to the world; the earth saw, and trembled.
verses.5: The mountains melted like wax at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.
verses.6: The heavens have declared his righteousness, and all the people have seen his glory.
verses.7: Let all that worship graven images be ashamed, who boast of their idols; worship him, all ye his angels.
verses.8: Sion heard and rejoiced; and the daughters of Judea exulted, because of thy judgments, O Lord.
verses.9: For thou art Lord most high over all the earth; thou art greatly exalted above all gods.
verses.10: Ye that love the Lord, hate evil; the Lord preserves the souls of his saints; he shall deliver them from the hand of sinners.
verses.11: Light is sprung up for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.
verses.12: Rejoice in the Lord, ye righteous; and give thanks for a remembrance of his holiness.

verses.1: A Psalm of David. Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great; thou hast clothed thyself with praise and honour:
verses.2: who dost robe thyself with light as with a garment; spreading out the heaven as a curtain.
verses.3: Who covers his chambers with waters; who makes the clouds his chariot; who walks on the wings of the wind.
verses.4: Who makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flaming fire.
verses.5: Who establishes the earth on her sure foundation: it shall not be moved for ever.
verses.6: The deep, as it were a garment, is his covering: the waters shall stand on the hills.
verses.7: At thy rebuke they shall flee; at the voice of thy thunder they shall be alarmed.
verses.8: They go up to the mountains, and down to the plains, to the place which thou hast founded for them.
verses.9: Thou hast set a bound which they shall not pass, neither shall they turn again to cover the earth.
verses.10: He sends forth his fountains among the valleys: the waters shall run between the mountains.
verses.11: They shall give drink to all the wild beasts of the field: the wild asses shall take of them to quench their thirst.
verses.12: By them shall the birds of the sky lodge: they shall utter a voice out of the midst of the rocks.
verses.13: He waters the mountains from his chambers: the earth shall be satisfied with the fruit of thy works.
verses.14: He makes grass to grow for the cattle, and green herb for the service of men, to bring bread out of the earth;
verses.15: and wine makes glad the heart of man, to make his face cheerful with oil: and bread strengthens man's heart.
verses.16: The trees of the plain shall be full of sap; even the cedars of Libanus which he has planted.
verses.17: There the sparrows will build their nests; and the house of the heron takes the lead among them.
verses.18: The high mountains are a refuge for the stags, and the rock for the rabbits.
verses.19: He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knows his going down.
verses.20: Thou didst make darkness, and it was night; in it all the wild beasts of the forest will be abroad:
verses.21: even young lions roaring for prey, and to seek meat for themselves from God.
verses.22: The sun arises, and they shall be gathered together, and shall lie down in their dens.
verses.23: Man shall go forth to his work, and to his labour till evening.
verses.24: How great are thy works, O Lord! in wisdom hast thou wrought them all: the earth is filled with thy creation.
verses.25: So is this great and wide sea: there are things creeping innumerable, small animals and great.
verses.26: There go the ships; and this dragon whom thou hast made to play in it.
verses.27: All wait upon thee, to give them their food in due season.
verses.28: When thou hast given it them, they will gather it; and when thou hast opened thine hand, they shall all be filled with good.
verses.29: But when thou hast turned away thy face, they shall be troubled: thou wilt take away their breath, and they shall fail, and return to their dust.
verses.30: Thou shalt send forth thy Spirit, and they shall be created; and thou shalt renew the face of the earth.
verses.31: Let the glory of the Lord be for ever: the Lord shall rejoice in his works;
verses.32: who looks upon the earth, and makes it tremble; who touches the mountains, and they smoke.
verses.33: I will sing to the Lord while I live; I will sing praise to my God while I exist.
verses.34: Let my meditation be sweet to him: and I will rejoice in the Lord.
verses.35: Let the sinners fail from off the earth, and transgressors, so that they shall be no more. Bless the Lord, O my soul.

verses.1: Alleluia. Give thanks to the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endures for ever.
verses.2: Let now the house of Israel say, that he is good: for his mercy endures for ever.
verses.3: Let now the house of Aaron say, that he is good: for his mercy endures for ever.
verses.4: Let now all that fear the Lord say, that he is good: for his mercy endures for ever.
verses.5: I called on the Lord out of affliction: and he hearkened to me, so as to bring me into a wide place.
verses.6: The Lord is my helper; and I will not fear what man shall do to me.
verses.7: The Lord is my helper; and I shall see my desire upon mine enemies.
verses.8: It is better to trust in the Lord than to trust in man.
verses.9: It is better to hope in the Lord, than to hope in princes.
verses.10: All nations compassed me about: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them.
verses.11: They completely compassed me about: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them.
verses.12: They compassed me about as bees do a honeycomb, and they burst into flame as fire among thorns: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them.
verses.13: I was thrust, and sorely shaken, that I might fall: but the Lord helped me.
verses.14: The Lord is my strength and my song, and is become my salvation.
verses.15: The voice of exultation and salvation is in the tabernacles of the righteous: the right hand of the Lord has wrought mightily.
verses.16: The right hand of the Lord has exalted me: the right hand of the Lord has wrought powerfully.
verses.17: I shall not die, but live, and recount the works of the Lord.
verses.18: The Lord has chastened me sore: but he has not given me up to death.
verses.19: Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and give praise to the Lord.
verses.20: This is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter by it.
verses.21: I will give thanks to thee; because thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation.
verses.22: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner.
verses.23: This has been done of the Lord; and it is wonderful in our eyes.
verses.24: This is the day which the Lord has made: let us exult and rejoice in it.
verses.25: O Lord, save now: O Lord, send now prosperity.
verses.26: Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord: we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord.
verses.27: God is the Lord, and he has shined upon us: celebrate the feast with thick branches, binding the victims even to the horns of the altar.
verses.28: Thou art my God, and I will give thee thanks: thou art my God, and I will exalt thee. I will give thanks to thee, for thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation.
verses.29: Give thanks to the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endures for ever.

verses.1: Alleluia. At the going forth of Israel from Egypt, of the house of Jacob from a barbarous people,
verses.2: Judea became his sanctuary, and Israel his dominion.
verses.3: The sea saw and fled: Jordan was turned back.
verses.4: The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like lambs.
verses.5: What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? and thou Jordan, that thou wast turned back?
verses.6: Ye mountains, that ye skipped like rams, and ye hills, like lambs?
verses.7: The earth trembled at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob;
verses.8: who turned the rock into pools of water, and the flint into fountains of water.
verses.9: Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to thy name give glory, because of thy mercy and thy truth;
verses.10: lest at any time the nations should say, Where is their God?
verses.11: But our God has done in heaven and on earth, whatsoever he has pleased.
verses.12: The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of men's hands.
verses.13: They have a mouth, but they cannot speak; they have eyes, but they cannot see:
verses.14: they have ears, but they cannot hear; they have noses, but they cannot smell;
verses.15: they have hands, but they cannot handle; they have feet, but they cannot walk: they cannot speak through their throat.
verses.16: Let those that make them become like to them, and all who trust in them.
verses.17: The house of Israel trusts in the Lord: he is their helper and defender.
verses.18: The house of Aaron trusts in the Lord: he is their helper and defender.
verses.19: They that fear the Lord trust in the Lord: he is their helper and defender.
